title: Rain and the Moon
checkpoint: Reception Spring 2, week 3 — Learning — Phase 3: new sounds ow, oi, ear
note_for_grown_ups: This book brings in the long-vowel teams ai, ee, igh, oa and oo (as in rain, keep, high, oak and moon). Say each team as one sound, not as two separate letters.

pages.illustration: Night rain falling hard across the whole page in long silver diagonals, the oak a dark mass behind it. No characters. Atmospheric and wet.

pages.text: Nell and Olive keep in the oak.
pages.illustration: Cutaway of the hollow in the oak: Nell and Olive tucked up dry inside, rain streaming past the opening. Warm inside, cold outside.
Close on a single leaf at the hollow's edge with rain running off it, and Nell's front leg reaching out into the drips. Cool blues and greens.
The rain visibly thinning — fewer, finer lines, a pale gap opening in the cloud. Same composition as page one so the change reads.
The clouds parting to show a big bright moon, Olive's face lifting towards it, her amber eyes catching the light.

pages.text: The moon is a big light.
pages.illustration: The moon drawn very large and pale, filling most of the page, the oak's bare top branches silhouetted across it.
Olive in profile on her branch, entirely still, moonlight on her round plum-coloured back. Quiet and dignified.
Closing page: Olive mid-hoot on the branch with Nell asleep in the crook below her. The whole wet garden shining in moonlight beneath them.
